util

Class RunCommand

  • java.lang.Object
    • util.RunCommand

  • public final class RunCommand
extends java.lang.Object
    Utility for executing external system commands and capturing combined output lines. Supports platform-independent command invocation (Unix/Linux/Windows). *

    Standard Error (stderr) is redirected to Standard Output (stdout) to prevent process deadlocks caused by unbuffered error streams. This ensures all process feedback is captured within a single list of results.

    Note: On Windows, built-in shell commands (such as dir or echo) must be invoked via cmd.exe /c.

      • addArgument

        public RunCommand addArgument(java.lang.String arg)
        Appends a single literal argument to the command. The argument is trimmed and added as a discrete token, ensuring spaces or special characters within the argument do not cause word-splitting.
        Parameters:
        arg - the argument string to add
        Returns:

      • execute

        public int execute()
            throws java.io.IOException
        Executes the command and captures its output. Standard Error (stderr) is merged into Standard Output (stdout) to prevent stream deadlocks.

        If the process hangs, it will be forcibly terminated after 30 seconds.

        Returns:
        the exit code of the process (typically 0 for success)
        Throws:
        java.io.IOException - if the execution fails, times out, or is interrupted

      • tokenize

        private static java.util.List<java.lang.String> tokenize(java.lang.String commandLine)
        Tokenises a command string into a list of arguments, preserving quoted strings and respecting backslash-escaped characters.

        Note: This method does not perform shell-specific expansions such as environment variable substitution, for example: $PATH or globbing *.txt.

        Parameters:
        commandLine - the full command string to tokenise
        Returns:
        a list of parsed tokens; an empty list if commandLine is null or empty
